New Rules at Sunshine Middle School

This term, Sunshine Middle School introduced several new rules, and they have caused a lot of discussion among students.

The first rule is about mobile phones. Students are not allowed to use phones during class time. If a teacher sees a student using a phone, the phone will be kept in the teacher's office until the end of the day. However, students can use their phones during lunch break and after school. "I think this rule is fair," said Wang Lei, a Grade 8 student. "It helps us pay more attention in class."

The second rule is about the school uniform. Students must wear uniforms from Monday to Thursday. On Fridays, they can wear their own clothes as long as they are appropriate for school. Many students like this change because they can express themselves on Fridays.

The third rule requires every student to join at least one after-school club. The school offers over twenty clubs, including basketball, art, music, robotics, and English drama. The headmaster believes that clubs help students develop interests outside of textbooks.

Not all students are happy with these changes. Some think the phone rule is too strict, while others complain that they have too much homework to join any club. The school says it will review the rules at the end of the term based on feedback from both students and teachers.

(1) When are students allowed to use mobile phones at school?
A. During class lessons and lunch breaks
B. Only during lunch breaks and after school
C. Anytime except Monday mornings
D. Whenever they need to call their parents

(2) What can students do on Fridays according to the new rules?
A. They don't need to come to school
B. They can choose not to wear uniforms
C. They must bring their club equipment
D. They are allowed to leave school early

(3) Why does the school require students to join a club?
A. To make more money for the school
B. To help students develop other interests
C. To prepare them for future competitions
D. To reduce the amount of free time

(4) Which of the following is TRUE about the new rules?
A. Every student thinks the rules are perfect
B. Teachers will decide all the rules alone
C. Some students have complaints about them
D. The rules will never change in the future

(5) What would be the best title for this passage?
A. Why Mobile Phones Are Bad for Students
B. How Clubs Help Students Get Better Grades
C. New Rules at Sunshine Middle School
D. What Students Should Wear to School
analysis:
(1) B【细节理解】第二段明确指出students can use phones during lunch break and after school；A选项during class与原文矛盾；C选项anytime except Monday过于宽泛；D选项whenever they need to call parents文中未提及
(2) B【细节理解】第三段提到On Fridays they can wear their own clothes即可以不穿校服；A选项不用上学错误；C和D文中未提及
(3) B【细节理解】第四段说明clubs help students develop interests outside of textbooks；A赚钱不是目的；C为比赛准备和D减少空闲时间均未提及
(4) C【推理判断】最后一段明确提到Some students think...too strict和others complain说明有学生不满；A与原文矛盾；B只由老师决定不对，文章说会review based on feedback；D永远不会改变太绝对
(5) C【主旨大意】全文围绕新校规展开讨论，涵盖手机、校服、社团三个方面；A、B、D都只是其中一个方面，以偏概全

question:
阅读下面短文。

A Bridge Between Generations

Li Hua, a 14-year-old girl, used to argue with her mother almost every day. Her mother always asked: "Have you finished your homework?" "Why is your room so messy?" "Why do you spend so much time on your phone?" Li Hua felt that her mother did not understand her at all.

Things changed last month when Li Hua's school organized a Parent-Child Communication Workshop. At the workshop, each pair of parent and child was given a special task: write a letter to each other about three things — one thing you appreciate about the other person, one thing you want the other person to understand, and one thing you hope to do together.

At first, Li Hua did not know what to write. But then she remembered how her mother always woke up early to prepare breakfast for her, even on cold winter mornings. She also thought about how her mother worried about her grades because she wanted her to have a good future. Slowly, tears came to her eyes as she wrote.

When she read her mother's letter, she cried again. Her mother wrote: "I know I ask too many questions sometimes. I just want you to know that I love you and I am proud of you." Her mother also admitted that she sometimes forgot that Li Hua was growing up and needed more space.

That evening, Li Hua and her mother sat down and talked for two hours — longer than they had talked in months. They made an agreement: Li Hua would keep her room tidy, and her mother would give her more freedom to manage her own time. Both sides felt much better after this honest conversation.

Experts say that many family problems come from poor communication. Taking time to listen and understand each other can build a stronger bridge between parents and children.

(1) What did Li Hua's mother usually ask her about?
A. Her friends and hobbies at school
B. Homework, room cleaning and phone use
C. What clothes she wanted to buy
D. Where she wanted to go for holidays

(2) What was the special task at the workshop?
A. To cook a meal together as a family
B. To take a test about parenting skills
C. To exchange letters about feelings and hopes
D. To plan a trip for the summer holiday

(3) Why did Li Hua cry when writing the letter?
A. She was angry with her mother
B. She realized how much her mother cared
C. The workshop was too boring for her
D. She could not think of anything to say

(4) What agreement did Li Hua and her mother reach?
A. Li Hua would move out of the house
B. Her mother would stop asking questions
C. Li Hua keeps tidy; Mother gives more space
D. They would go to the workshop weekly

(5) What does the writer want to tell us through this story?
A. Mothers should not ask too many questions
B. Teenagers need more freedom than adults
C. Good communication helps solve family problems
D. Workshops are better than talking at home
analysis:
(1) B【细节理解】第一段列举了母亲的三个问题：作业、房间乱、玩手机时间多；A朋友爱好、C买衣服、D去度假均未在第一段出现
(2) C【细节理解】第二段明确写write a letter about three things——感激/理解/希望一起做的事；A做饭、B考试、D旅行均未提及
(3) B【推理判断】第三段描述她想起母亲早起做早餐等细节后slowly, tears came——是因为感受到了母亲的关爱；A生气与tears的语境不符；C无聊和D想不出内容都不是哭的原因
(4) C【细节理解】第四段明确写了双方约定：Li Hua保持整洁，母亲给更多自由空间；A搬出去和B不再问问题都未提及；D每周去workshop没有依据
(5) C【主旨大意】最后一段是点睛之笔：many family problems come from poor communication，强调沟通的重要性；A和B都是片面观点；D workshops better than home talking文中并未比较

question:

The Art of Making Friends

Making true friends is one of the most important skills we need in life. But how exactly do we make friends? Here are some useful tips from psychologists.

First, be a good listener. When someone talks to you, really listen. Put down your phone, look at the person, and show interest in what they are saying. Most people enjoy talking about themselves, so if you let others share their thoughts and feelings, they will feel valued and want to spend more time with you.

Second, find common interests. Friends often become close because they enjoy doing things together. It could be sports, music, reading, or video games. If you join a club or a team, you will naturally meet people who like the same things you do.

Third, be honest and kind. True friendship is built on trust. If you make a mistake, say sorry. If a friend needs help, offer your support. Small acts of kindness — lending a pen, sharing notes, or simply smiling — can make a big difference in how people see you.

Fourth, learn to handle disagreements. No two people agree on everything. When you disagree with a friend, stay calm. Do not shout or say hurtful words. Instead, explain your point of view respectfully and try to find a solution that works for both of you.

Finally, remember that making friends takes time. You cannot become best friends with someone after just one conversation. Be patient, keep trying, and the right people will come into your life.

(1) What does the writer suggest doing when others are speaking?
A. Think about what you want to say next
B. Look at your phone and check messages
C. Put away distractions and pay attention
D. Change the topic to something more fun

(2) According to the passage, why should you join a club?
A. To get better grades in all subjects
B. To meet people who share your interests
C. To show everyone how talented you are
D. To avoid spending time at home alone

(3) What builds trust between friends according to the text?
A. Giving expensive gifts to each other
B. Always agreeing with everything said
C. Being honest, kind and offering help
D. Keeping secrets from other people

(4) What should you do when you disagree with a friend?
A. Shout louder than the other person
B. Stop talking to them completely
C. Explain your view calmly and respectfully
D. Ask a teacher to decide who is right

(5) What is the main purpose of this passage?
A. To explain why some people have no friends
B. To give advice on how to make and keep friends
C. To compare different types of friendships
D. To describe problems between teenagers
analysis:
(1) C【细节理解】第二段明确Put down your phone, look at the person, show interest——即放下干扰专注听；A想下一句说什么是不专心表现；B看手机正好相反；D换话题不礼貌
(2) B【细节理解】第三段you will naturally meet people who like the same things；A提高成绩不是目的；C展示才华和D避免独处均非加入社团的主要原因
(3) C【细节理解】第四段True friendship is built on trust，接着列举honest/sorry/help/kindness；A送贵重礼物不是建立信任的方式；B永远同意和D保守秘密都不是文章提到的信任基础
(4) C【细节理解】第五段explain your point of view respectfully；A大喊大叫和D找老师评判都与calmly/respectfully矛盾；B完全停止交流更不可取
(5) B【主旨大意】全文围绕交友技巧展开（听/共同兴趣/诚实/处理分歧），属于建议类说明文；A解释为什么没朋友只在开头暗示但非重点；C比较不同友谊类型和D描述青少年问题均不符合全文结构

Secrets of Top Students

What makes some students consistently get good grades while others struggle? Researchers have found that intelligence is only part of the answer. Study habits play a much bigger role than most people realize.

The most successful students follow a regular schedule. They study at the same time every day, usually in a quiet place without distractions such as TV or phones. Studies show that our brains work better when they know when to expect learning activities. One top student, Zhang Ming, says he reviews his lessons every evening from 7:00 to 9:00 PM, no matter what.

Another key habit is taking good notes. Top students do not try to write down everything the teacher says. Instead, they focus on key words, main ideas, and examples. After class, they quickly go over their notes while the information is still fresh in their minds. Research shows that reviewing within 24 hours can help you remember 80% more information.

Successful students also know how to take breaks. The human brain cannot focus well for long periods. Scientists recommend studying for 25 minutes and then resting for 5 minutes. This method, called the Pomodoro Technique, has helped millions of students around the world improve their efficiency.

Finally, getting enough sleep is essential. Many students stay up late to study, but this actually hurts their performance. Lack of sleep makes it harder to concentrate and remember things. Doctors recommend that teenagers sleep at least 8 hours every night. Your brain needs rest to store what you have learned during the day.

(1) What does research say about intelligence and study success?
A. Intelligence is the only factor that matters
B. Intelligence matters less than study habits
C. Smart students never need to study hard
D. Study habits are not important for grades

(2) When does Zhang Ming usually review his lessons?
A. Early in the morning before school
B. During lunch break at school
C. From 7 to 9 PM every evening
D. Right before he goes to sleep

(3) Why do top students focus on key words instead of everything?
A. Because teachers speak too fast to catch all
B. Because they want notes that are easy to review
C. Because they are too lazy to write more
D. Because they cannot read their own writing

(4) How long does the Pomodoro Technique suggest studying at a time?
A. For 60 minutes without stopping
B. For 25 minutes followed by a short break
C. For as long as you feel like studying
D. For 5 minutes between each class period

(5) What happens when students do not get enough sleep?
A. They become smarter and learn faster
B. Their concentration and memory suffer
C. They finish their homework more quickly
D. They do not need to study as much
analysis:
(1) B【细节理解】第一段intelligence is only part... habits play a much bigger role——智力只是一部分，习惯作用更大；A唯一因素与only part矛盾；C聪明的学生不需要努力和D习惯不重要都与原文相反
(2) C【细节理解】第二段reviews his lessons every evening from 7:00 to 9:00 PM；A早上、B午休、D睡前均不符
(3) B【推理判断】第二段提到focus on key words, main ideas之后紧接着reviewing within 24 hours can help remember 80% more——记关键词是为了便于复习回顾效率更高；A老师说太快和C懒惰D看不清自己的字都没有根据
(4) B【细节理解】第三段studying for 25 minutes and then resting for 5 minutes；A不停学60分钟正好相反；C想学多久就学多久和D每节课间5分钟都不对
(5) B【细节理解】最后一段Lack of sleep makes it harder to concentrate and remember things；A变聪明和C更快完成作业都反了；D不需要多学了也不对

Why Exercise Matters More Than You Think

We all know exercise is good for us, but do you know exactly how good? Recent studies show that regular physical activity benefits not only your body but also your mind and emotions.

Physically, exercise strengthens your heart and lungs. When you run, swim, or play basketball, your heart beats faster and pumps more blood throughout your body. Over time, this makes your heart stronger and reduces the risk of heart disease later in life. Exercise also helps build strong bones and muscles, which is especially important for teenagers whose bodies are still growing.

Mentally, exercise can improve your brain function. Research shows that students who exercise regularly tend to get better grades than those who do not. Why? Physical activity increases blood flow to the brain and helps create new brain cells. It also improves memory and focus. So if you are having trouble concentrating on your homework, going for a quick run might actually help!

Emotionally, exercise is one of the best ways to reduce stress. When you exercise, your body releases chemicals called endorphins (内啡肽). These natural chemicals make you feel happier and more relaxed. That is why many people say they feel better after a workout, even if they were feeling down before.

Health experts recommend that teenagers get at least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous exercise every day. This does not mean you have to spend hours in a gym. Walking to school, riding a bike, playing soccer with friends, or even dancing in your room all count!

(1) How does exercise affect the heart according to the passage?
A. It makes the heart beat slower and weaker
B. It strengthens the heart and reduces disease risk
C. It only helps older people, not teenagers
D. It causes heart problems if done too much

(2) Why might exercising students get better grades?
A. They have more time to study after sports
B. Their teachers like active students more
C. Physical activity boosts blood flow to the brain
D. They are naturally smarter than other kids

(3) What are endorphins according to the text?
A. Chemicals that make you feel tired and weak
B. Substances released during exercise that improve mood
C. A type of medicine for treating stress
D. Foods that give you energy for sports

(4) How much daily exercise do health experts suggest for teens?
A. About 15 minutes of light walking per day
B. At least one hour of activity every day
C. Two hours of gym training each week
D. As much as possible without getting tired

(5) Which activity would NOT count as recommended exercise?
A. Riding a bike to school
B. Dancing in your bedroom
C. Playing soccer with classmates
D. Sitting and watching sports on TV

(1) B【细节理解】第二段makes your heart stronger and reduces the risk of heart disease；A更慢更弱与stronger矛盾；C只帮老人不对，后面说especially important for teenagers；D运动太多导致心脏病文中没提
(2) C【细节理解】第三段increases blood flow to the brain and helps create new brain cells；A有更多时间学习不是原因——运动反而占用了学习时间；B老师更喜欢和D天生更聪明都没根据
(3) B【词义猜测】第四段chemicals called endorphins...make you feel happier and more relaxed——内啡肽是运动时释放的让人快乐的化学物质；A让人累弱的正好相反；C治疗压力的药不对；D给能量的食物也不是
(4) B【细节理解】最后一段at least 60 minutes = 至少一小时；A15分钟太少；C两小时每周不够具体；D尽可能多不太准确，专家建议的是至少一小时
(5) D【推理判断】最后一段列举walking/biking/soccer/dancing all count——坐着看电视体育节目不算体育锻炼；A骑车上学、B跳舞、C踢球都算

My Unforgettable Trip to Yunnan

Last summer holiday, my parents took me to Yunnan Province for a seven-day trip. It was my first time visiting this beautiful southwestern region of China, and I fell in love with it immediately.

Our first stop was Kunming, known as the "Spring City" because of its pleasant weather all year round. We visited the Stone Forest, a amazing natural wonder with thousands of tall rocks that look like trees, animals, and even people. Our guide told us stories about how each rock got its shape. Some shapes were so funny that we could not stop laughing.

Next, we took a train to Dali. The old town there was full of traditional buildings, small shops selling handmade crafts, and restaurants serving delicious local food. I tried a special noodle dish called "crossing-the-bridge noodles," which has an interesting story behind its name. The streets were lined with flowers, and many tourists liked to ride bicycles along Erhai Lake to enjoy the scenery.

From Dali, we traveled to Lijiang, famous for its waterways and wooden bridges. The old town of Lijiang is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In the evenings, local Naxi people played traditional music in the squares, and visitors joined them in dancing. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming.

The highlight of our trip was seeing Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. Even in July, the peak was covered in snow. Standing at over 4,000 meters above sea level, I felt tiny compared to nature's grandeur. This trip taught me that traveling is not just about seeing new places — it is about experiencing different cultures and understanding how diverse and wonderful our world truly is.

(1) Why is Kunming called the "Spring City"?
A. Because flowers bloom there all year long
B. Because its weather is pleasant in every season
C. Because it is located near a hot spring
D. Because spring is the best time to visit it

(2) What is special about the Stone Forest?
A. It has thousands of unusually shaped rock formations
B. It is the largest forest in all of China
C. It was built by ancient people long ago
D. It is famous for its colorful flower gardens

(3) What did the writer eat in Dali?
A. Hot pot with spicy Sichuan flavors
B. Rice dumplings for the Dragon Boat Festival
C. A local noodle dish called crossing-the-bridge noodles
D. Fresh seafood caught from Erhai Lake

(4) What can tourists do in Lijiang in the evenings?
A. Go skiing on the snow mountain
B. Watch traditional music and join in dancing
C. Shop for modern clothes in big malls
D. Stay inside hotels because it is dangerous outside

(5) What did the writer learn from this trip?
A. Traveling is too expensive for most families
B. Natural wonders are more interesting than cities
C. Travel helps us experience cultures and see diversity
D. Seven days is too short for any meaningful trip

(2) A【细节理解】第二段thousands of tall rocks that look like trees, animals, and even people——成千上万形状各异的岩石；B中国最大的森林不对，它不是森林是石林；C古人建造的和D花园都不符合Stone Forest的特点
(3) C【细节理解】第三段tried a special noodle dish called "crossing-the-bridge noodles"；A火锅是四川特色；B粽子端午节食物不是大理特产；D海鲜Erhai Lake虽有大理但作者吃的是过桥米线
(4) B【细节理解】第四段played traditional music...visitors joined them in dancing；A滑雪是在玉龙雪山不是晚上古城里的事；C大商场买现代服装不是古城特色；D外面危险住酒店毫无根据
(5) C【主旨大意】最后一段traveling is not just about seeing places—it is about experiencing cultures and understanding diversity；A太贵、B自然比城市有趣、D七天太短都不是文章要传达的信息

The Hidden Language of Elephants

Elephants are the largest land animals on Earth, but there is much more to them than their size. These gentle giants have complex social lives and surprising ways of communicating.

Elephants live in family groups led by the oldest female, called the matriarch (女族长). She knows where to find food and water, remembers dangers from the past, and teaches younger elephants how to survive. When a member of the group dies, elephants have been seen touching the body with their trunks and standing silently around it — behavior that suggests they may experience something similar to grief.

One way elephants communicate is through sounds that humans cannot hear. They produce very low-frequency rumbles (低频隆鸣声) that can travel through the ground for several kilometers. Other elephants can feel these vibrations (震动) through their feet. Scientists believe this allows them to warn each other about danger or call family members from far away.

Elephants also communicate through body language. Flapping their ears can mean excitement or an attempt to cool down. Touching trunks is a sign of greeting or affection. Raising the trunk high usually means the elephant is alert and checking its surroundings.

Sadly, elephants face serious threats. People hunt them for their ivory (象牙), and their living spaces are shrinking due to human activities. Conservation groups are working hard to protect these amazing animals. Some countries have banned ivory trading, and national parks provide safe areas where elephants can live peacefully. Everyone can help by refusing to buy products made from ivory.

(1) Who leads an elephant family group?
A. The strongest male in the group
B. The oldest female called matriarch
C. The elephant with the biggest ears
D. The one that finds food fastest

(2) What behavior suggests elephants may feel grief?
A. Running away from dead bodies quickly
B. Eating more food when a member dies
C. Touching the body and standing silently
D. Making loud noises to scare predators

(3) How do elephants send messages over long distances?
A. By writing symbols on tree bark
B. Through low-frequency ground vibrations
C. By sending signals via satellites
D. Using mirrors to reflect sunlight

(4) What does raising the trunk high usually mean?
A. The elephant wants to fight
B. It feels sleepy and ready to rest
C. The elephant is alert and observing
D. It is trying to hide from danger

(5) What can ordinary people do to help elephants?
A. Keep elephants as pets at home
B. Visit national parks only in winter
C. Refuse to purchase any ivory products
D. Donate large amounts of money monthly

(1) B【细节理解】第二段led by the oldest female, called the matriarch——由最年长的雌性领导；A最强壮的雄性不对，象群是母系社会；C耳朵最大和D找食物最快都不对
(2) C【细节理解】第二段touching the body with their trunks and standing silently around it——触碰尸体静立周围；A快速跑开和C吃更多以及D发出大声吓捕食者都不是描述的行为
(3) B【细节理解】第三段low-frequency rumbles...travel through the ground...feel these vibrations through their feet——低频声通过地面传播；A树皮符号、C卫星信号、D反射阳光都不是大象通讯方式
(4) C【细节理解】第四段raising the trunk high usually means the elephant is alert and checking surroundings——警觉观察环境；A想打架、B困了想休息、D躲藏危险都不符
(5) C【细节理解】最后一段refusing to buy products made from ivory；A养宠物不对；B冬天参观公园无关；D每月捐大钱不是普通人都能做到的

Two Festivals, Two Cultures

Festivals are windows into a culture's traditions and values. Let's compare two important festivals — Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival and American Thanksgiving.

The Mid-Autumn Festival falls on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month, usually in September or October. Families gather together to admire the full moon, which represents reunion (团圆). The traditional food is mooncakes, round pastries filled with sweet or savory ingredients. Children love carrying colorful lanterns and listening to the legend of Chang'e flying to the moon. The festival emphasizes family togetherness and gratitude for the harvest.

Thanksgiving is celebrated on the fourth Thursday in November in the United States. It originated from a feast shared by early settlers and Native Americans in 1621. The traditional meal includes roast turkey, mashed potatoes, pumpkin pie, and cranberry sauce. Families travel long distances to be together. Before eating, many people share what they are thankful for. Watching football games and parades on TV are also popular activities.

Although these festivals come from different cultures, they share important common values: both celebrate family reunions, both involve special foods, and both encourage people to express thanks for what they have. The main difference lies in their origins — one is based on the lunar calendar and ancient legends, while the other marks a historical event of cooperation between different peoples.

Understanding festivals from around the world helps us respect cultural differences and discover what all humans share: the need to connect with loved ones and celebrate life together.

(1) When is the Mid-Autumn Festival celebrated?
A. On the first day of January each year
B. On the 15th day of the 8th lunar month
C. On the fourth Thursday of November
D. Whenever the full moon appears brightest

(2) What does the full moon symbolize in Chinese culture?
A. The beginning of a new harvest season

The Art of Chinese Paper Cutting

Chinese paper cutting, or Jianzhi (剪纸), is one of the oldest and most popular folk arts in China. With a pair of scissors and a piece of red paper, skilled artists can create amazing designs — flowers, animals, characters, and scenes from daily life and traditional stories.

The history of paper cutting dates back over 1,500 years to the Northern and Southern Dynasties. At first, it was used mainly for religious purposes and as decorations during festivals. Red is the most commonly used color because it symbolizes joy, luck, and happiness in Chinese culture. During the Spring Festival, nearly every household in northern China decorates windows and doors with red paper cuttings.

Making paper cuttings requires patience and precision. The artist folds the paper multiple times to create symmetrical patterns, then carefully cuts along the drawn lines. One small mistake can ruin the whole design. Beginners usually start with simple patterns like snowflakes or basic flowers, while master artists can cut extremely detailed works with hundreds of connected pieces that must not break apart.

Paper cutting designs carry symbolic meanings. Fish represent abundance because the word for fish (鱼) sounds like surplus (余). Peaches symbolize longevity (长寿). Dragons and phoenixes stand for power and good fortune. Double happiness characters (囍) are used at weddings to wish couples a joyful marriage.

Today, paper cutting is not just a traditional craft — it has become a bridge between Chinese culture and the world. Chinese paper cutting was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage List in 2009. Artists now combine traditional techniques with modern ideas, creating paper cuttings that appeal to young people and international audiences alike.

Eating Smart: A Guide for Teenagers

As a teenager, your body is growing fast, and what you eat plays a huge role in how you feel and perform. Yet many students skip breakfast, rely on junk food, or go on unhealthy diets to lose weight. Let's look at what science tells us about smart eating.

Breakfast truly is the most important meal of the day. After sleeping for 8 hours, your body needs fuel to start functioning. Studies show that students who eat breakfast concentrate better in class, score higher on tests, and have healthier body weights than those who skip it. A good breakfast includes protein (eggs, milk, tofu), whole grains (oats, whole wheat bread), and some fruit. Even a banana and a cup of milk are far better than nothing.

Sugar is everywhere — in sodas, candies, snacks, and even some "healthy" drinks. While sugar tastes good, too much of it leads to energy crashes, weight gain, and tooth decay. The WHO recommends that teenagers consume no more than 25 grams of added sugar per day — that is about six teaspoons. Next time you reach for a soda, check the label first.

Vegetables and fruits should fill half of your plate at each meal. They provide vitamins, minerals, and fiber that your body needs. Different colored vegetables contain different nutrients, so eat a variety — dark green leafy vegetables, red tomatoes, orange carrots, purple eggplant. If you dislike vegetables, try cooking them differently: roasting, stir-frying, or adding them to soups.

Finally, drink enough water. Your body is about 60% water, and even mild dehydration (脱水) can cause headaches, tiredness, and difficulty focusing. Carry a water bottle and sip throughout the day. Aim for about 8 glasses (roughly 2 liters) daily.

(1) Why is breakfast important for students?

A. No more than about 25 grams or six teaspoons

Staying Safe on the Road

Every day, millions of students travel to and from school. Whether you walk, cycle, take a bus, or ride in a car, knowing traffic safety rules can protect you from danger.

For walkers, the golden rule is simple: use crosswalks and obey traffic lights. Never assume that drivers can see you — especially when crossing from behind parked cars or large buses. Make eye contact with drivers before stepping into the road. Also, avoid looking at your phone while walking near traffic. Studies show that distracted walking causes thousands of accidents each year.

Cyclists face additional risks. Always wear a helmet — it can reduce the risk of head injury by up to 85%. Ride on bike lanes where available, and follow the same direction as cars. Use hand signals before turning so drivers know what you plan to do. Never weave in and out of traffic or ride against the flow. At night, wear reflective clothing and make sure your bike has front and rear lights.

If you take a bus, wait at the designated stop, not on the road. Board and exit in an orderly manner — do not push or crowd. Once on the bus, hold onto handrails, especially when the vehicle is moving. Save the headphone-wearing and phone-scrolling for when you are safely seated or off the bus. And never run after a moving bus!

For those who ride electric scooters (电动滑板车), which have become popular among teenagers recently: wear protective gear including knee pads and elbow pads. Follow speed limits — most areas limit scooter speeds to 15-20 km/h. Remember that you are smaller and harder for drivers to see than cars. Ride defensively and assume others may not notice you.

Navigating the Online World Safely

The internet is an incredible tool for learning, entertainment, and connecting with others. But it also has risks that every teenager needs to understand and guard against.

Personal information protection is the first rule. Never post your home address, phone number, school name, or detailed daily schedule on social media. Even posting a photo in front of your school with your uniform on can reveal your location. Cybercriminals can use small pieces of information to build a complete profile of you. Set your accounts to private and only accept friend requests from people you actually know.

Phishing (钓鱼) scams are another danger. You might receive an email or message saying you have won a prize or that your account will be closed unless you click a link and enter your password. Legitimate companies never ask for passwords through email or messages. When in doubt, go directly to the official website instead of clicking links in messages. If something looks too good to be true, it probably is.

Cyberbullying (网络欺凌) affects millions of teenagers worldwide. It includes spreading rumors, posting hurtful comments, sharing embarrassing photos, or excluding someone from online groups. If you are being bullied, do not respond to the bully — that is exactly what they want. Instead, screenshot the evidence, block the person, and report it to a trusted adult or platform. Remember: what happens online stays online forever. A moment of cruelty can follow someone for years.

Finally, manage your screen time wisely. Spending too much time online can affect your sleep, eyesight, mood, and academic performance. Try setting limits — for example, no screens one hour before bed. Take regular breaks and make time for offline activities: sports, reading, hobbies, and face-to-face interactions with friends and family.

Why Arts Education Matters

In many schools, when budgets get tight, art and music programs are often the first to be cut. Administrators argue that students need more time for math, science, and test preparation. But research increasingly shows that cutting arts education may be a serious mistake.

Studies have found that students who participate in arts programs perform better academically overall. Learning music, for example, strengthens areas of the brain involved in language processing and mathematical reasoning. One study followed students who learned to play instruments and found that their reading and math scores improved significantly compared to students who did not. The discipline of practicing an instrument also teaches patience, persistence, and attention to detail.

Visual arts develop different but equally important skills. Drawing, painting, and sculpture train students to observe carefully, think creatively, and express ideas visually. These skills are valuable in many careers — architecture, graphic design, engineering, and even medicine (where doctors need keen observational skills).

Beyond academic benefits, arts education supports emotional development. Creating art allows students to express feelings that they might struggle to put into words. Performing in a choir or theater group builds confidence and teamwork skills. For shy students, acting on stage can be a transformative experience that helps them find their voice.

Critics argue that not every student will become a professional artist or musician. This is true — but that is not the point. The goal of arts education is not to produce professionals. It is to develop well-rounded individuals who can think creatively, appreciate beauty, and express themselves. In a world where AI can handle many technical tasks, these human qualities become more valuable, not less.

Understanding Climate Change: What Every Teenager Should Know

You have probably heard adults talk about "global warming" or "climate change" on the news. But what does it really mean, and why should you care? Let's break it down in simple terms.

The earth has a natural greenhouse effect. Gases in the atmosphere — mainly carbon dioxide (CO2) — trap heat from the sun, keeping our planet warm enough for life. Without this effect, Earth would be frozen and uninhabitable. The problem is that human activities are adding extra CO2 to the atmosphere. Burning fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) for energy, cutting down forests, and raising farm animals all release CO2. More CO2 means more heat trapped — like putting on an extra blanket that you cannot take off.

So what is happening? The average global temperature has risen by about 1.1°C since pre-industrial times. This does not sound like much, but it has big effects: glaciers (冰川) are melting, sea levels are rising, extreme weather events (heatwaves, floods, droughts) are becoming more frequent and severe, and some animal species are losing their habitats.

Scientists warn that if temperatures rise above 1.5°C, the consequences could be much worse. Coastal cities could face regular flooding. Food production could drop in many regions. Diseases spread by insects could expand to new areas. The good news is that it is not too late to act. Countries around the world have agreed to reduce emissions. Renewable energy sources like solar and wind power are becoming cheaper. Electric vehicles are replacing gas-powered cars.

As a teenager, you might wonder what you can do. Actually, plenty! Reduce energy use at home, choose public transport, eat less meat, reduce waste, and most importantly — speak up. Climate action starts with understanding and caring.

(1) What is the natural greenhouse effect?
A. A process that freezes the entire planet
B. Atmospheric gases trapping solar heat for warmth

D. The cooling effect of polar ice caps

(2) What human activity adds extra CO2 to the atmosphere?
A. Planting more trees in empty lands
B. Using wind and solar energy sources

D. Disease-spreading insects will disappear

(5) What does the writer suggest teenagers can do about climate change?

B. Reduce personal carbon footprint and raise awareness
C. Wait for governments to solve everything alone
D. Focus only on economic development goals
analysis:
(1) B【细节理解】第二段Gases in the atmosphere trap heat from the sun, keeping planet warm enough——大气气体捕获太阳热量使地球温暖宜居；A冻结整个星球正好相反；C去除CO2的方法和D极地冰层降温效应都不对
